prompt_text: Where should I buy tires in Pleasanton CA and who does the best installation?
answer_verbatim:
I can give a short list of likely good options in Pleasanton plus a checklist to pick the best installer. To give specific shop names and current prices I can look up, tell me your vehicle (make/model/year) and tire size or whether you want all-season, performance, or winter tires.

General recommendations and how to choose

1) National chains (good if you want predictable pricing, selection, and warranty service)
- Discount Tire / America’s Tire — large selection, usually excellent mounting/balancing, lifetime rotations on some tires, well-reviewed installers.
- Costco Tire Center — very competitive tire pricing and good value on mounting/installation; must be a Costco member; limited brands but good deals and solid service.
- Firestone Complete Auto Care / Mavis / Pep Boys — wide availability, often run promotions, good for same-day service and alignments.

Pros: standardized processes, nationwide warranties, easy scheduling.
Cons: can be busier, upsells, installation fees vary.

2) Local independent shops (best for personalized service, possible lower labor fees, and local reputation)
- Independents can offer brand recommendations tailored to your driving needs, often do careful mounting and will work with you if there is an issue.
- Look for ASE-certified technicians and shops with lots of recent 4–5 star Google/Yelp reviews.

3) How to pick the best installer (short checklist to ask/verify)
- Certifications: ASE, AAA approval, or manufacturer endorsements.
- Included services: mounting, balanced, new valve stems, tire disposal fee, TPMS reprogramming (if applicable).
- Alignment: ask whether a wheel alignment is recommended/included — new tires generally do best after alignment.
- Warranty & road-hazard protection: price and length; is road-hazard optional and worth the cost?
- Tools & process: do they use computerized balancers and proper torque specs for lug nuts?
- Reviews: recent Google and Yelp reviews mentioning installation quality, balancing, and post-install issues.
- Price transparency: get a written or emailed quote including all fees and estimated wait time.

4) Practical tips
- Get 2–3 quotes (include installation costs, disposal, valve stems, TPMS).
- Ask whether they match prices from other local shops.
- If you have AWD/4WD or performance tires, insist on a proper alignment and high-quality mounting/balancing.
- Schedule an alignment within a few hundred miles of new tires if recommended.

Next step
Tell me your car make/model/year and tire size or what kind of tire you want (all-season, performance, winter), and whether you prefer a national chain or an independent shop. I’ll give a more specific short list of recommended shops in Pleasanton and what to ask each one.
